subject: Reactivation request: lapsed evaluation credits for Lumos pilot
messages:
From: Emily Park <emily@lumos.ai>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 5 Feb 2027 15:22:00 -0000
Subject: Request to reopen expired evaluation credits for Lumos pilot

Hi Rishi,

Hope you’re well — I’m Emily Park, Head of Platform at Lumos AI. We kicked off a small pilot with Redwood back in October, but hiring and budget freezes delayed our internal evaluation and our promo credits expired last month.

We still want to complete the evaluation (generative summarization + embeddings for 3M tokens over a month). Is there any way to get a one-off reactivation or short extension of the promo credits so we can finish the end-to-end testing? We’d be happy to sign a short MOU or accept a usage cap.

High-level ask: re-open 30 days / up to 3M tokens. We’re targeting a production decision by end of March.

Thanks for considering — I can share the pilot test plan if that helps.

— Emily Park
Head of Platform, Lumos AI
emily@lumos.ai | (415) 555-0147


From: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Park <emily@lumos.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 5 Feb 2027 17:03:15 -0000
Subject: Re: Request to reopen expired evaluation credits for Lumos pilot

Thanks Emily — and appreciate the context. I’m reviewing this with our pilot approvals process. A couple quick clarifying Qs so I can move this forward to the AM/ops team: 

1) Which features in the pilot are must-have (generation, embeddings, or both)?
2) Do you need the original model variant we provisioned, or are you ok with a slightly lower-cost quantized variant if that helps with limits?
3) Is Lumos willing to sign a short MOU and accept a usage cap/expiration date (we usually do 30-day one-offs or a 50% token cap on the original allocation)?

I’ve looped in Marissa (AM) to assess customer fit and Sean on the approvals side for a one-time credit reinstatement. If you can confirm the three points, I’ll propose a one-off plan back today.

— Rishi
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 5 Feb 2027 18:10:02 -0000
Subject: Re: Request to reopen expired evaluation credits for Lumos pilot

Looping in details from our side — Lumos did an initial POC in Oct (3 seats, telemetry integrated). They showed good signal on embeddings recall but didn’t complete the generation validation. If we offer a timebound reactivation I recommend: 

- 30 days reactivation
- Hard cap: 3,000,000 tokens (matching Emily’s ask)
- Model variant: rdm-7b-std or rdm-7b-quad-lite (customer to pick)
- Require signed MOU confirming testing scope and data handling (no production data)

If compliance ops signs off on the MOU we can support this as a one-time goodwill. Sean — can you confirm we have approval bandwidth and whether we need a legal ticket?

— Marissa
Senior AM, Redwood Inference

From: Emily Park <emily@lumos.ai>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 8 Feb 2027 13:42:30 -0000
Subject: Re: Request to reopen expired evaluation credits for Lumos pilot

Rishi / Marissa — thanks for the quick responses and the thoughtful proposal. Confirming details below: 

- Must-have: embeddings pipeline + a small generation route for prompt validation (both)
- Model: happy to start on rdm-7b-quad-lite to keep costs reasonable; may request rdm-7b-std later if we need quality comparisons
- MOU: yes, we’ll sign a short MOU. We can restrict to synthetic or anonymized records as requested (no raw customer PII).

If you can provision 30 days up to 3,000,000 tokens and send the MOU, I’ll get it signed today. We aim to run key evals in the first two weeks.

— Emily

From: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, Emily Park <emily@lumos.ai>
Date: Tue, 9 Feb 2027 18:05:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Request to reopen expired evaluation credits for Lumos pilot

Thanks all — approvals granted under the one-off policy. Summary of decision and next steps: 

- Approved: 30-day reactivation, hard cap 3,000,000 tokens, model variant rdm-7b-quad-lite by default.
- Requirements: signed MOU and a short checklist confirming no production PII will be used.
- Ops action: 1) Provision a promo code that applies exactly 3,000,000 tokens and expires in 30 days. 2) Attach the one-off MOU (stubbed here).

Emily — I’ve created the promo code: LUMOS-30D-3M-TOKENS. It’s active once MOU is signed and returned to legal@redwood.ai. I attached the MOU draft for signature (MOU-Lumos-OneOff.pdf). Once legal has the signed copy we’ll flip the switch.

Attachments: MOU-Lumos-OneOff.pdf (pdf, 45KB)

— Sean Gallagher
Head of Customer Ops, Redwood Inference
